articles.title: ‘Halloweenmas’: how the spooky one-nighter turned into a month-long spectacular
articles.summary: Welcome to Halloweenmas, weeks of themed fun and gifts – from costume parties to decorating trees – without the stress, rules or cost of Christmas. The tree is up, the wreath is hanging on the front door and you’ve just opened your advent calendar.
body: If it sounds like the stuff of nightmares then that’s the point: Britons are increasingly decorating their homes with ghoulish versions of Christmas traditions. Think of it as Halloweenmas.

“What was traditionally a single-night celebration has turned into a month-long event mirroring many of Christmas’s traditions, but without the same level of expectation,” said Charlotte Broadbent, the UK general manager for the online wholesale platform Faire.

Analysis of thousands of sales transactions on the platform revealed a huge rise in the number of Halloweenmas products available – up more than 500% in the past four years, from 425 in 2021 to 2,632 in 2025. The biggest areas of growth are trees, wreaths and ornaments.
According to the budget retailer Wilko, Halloween trees are one of the biggest decorating trends of 2026. It said sales of artificial trees were 200% higher in September than a year ago.
points: Welcome to Halloweenmas, weeks of themed fun and gifts – from costume parties to decorating trees – without the stress, rules or cost of Christmas.
The tree is up, the wreath is hanging on the front door and you’ve just opened your advent calendar.

articles.title: The hill I will die on: Pumpkin-spiced latte is a con. It’s time to put an end to Big Autumn | Chloë Hamilton
articles.summary: The aesthetic of crisp mornings and roaring fireplaces has created a personality driven by social media. Let’s just admit the reality: mud, drizzle and shorter days. It’s getting earlier every year, that first meme about golden leaves and pumpkin-spiced lattes.
body: Because, of course, for those that like crisp mornings, Halloween and glasses of red wine in front of roaring fires, the arrival of autumn brings with it something else: the incessant need to tell everyone just how much they love this perfectly pleasant, if perpetually damp, season.

I call it Big Autumn. The idea that liking autumn is enough to sustain an entire personality. I don’t know when it first happened but my instinct is that it’s been driven by an almost entirely brown-and-orange aesthetic pushed out via Pinterest and Instagram, and not by the often grim realities: grey drizzle, shorter days, the sense of impending Christmas.

It’s not that I have an issue with the season itself. Sure, my partner and I refer to it as “mud season” because we have a spaniel and two young children, and our house won’t feel truly clean again until the end of March. But I’m partial to a roast dinner and a fairy light, I like oversized jumpers and, although I avoid Halloween, I find Bonfire Night quite magical, even if I do always over-layer and end up sweaty and overstimulated.
points: The aesthetic of crisp mornings and roaring fireplaces has created a personality driven by social media.
Let’s just admit the reality: mud, drizzle and shorter days.

articles.title: My partner’s obnoxious conduct at our sons’ football matches is putting me off him | Annalisa Barbieri
articles.summary: His behaviour is certainly inappropriate, but take a quiet moment to try to find out where the anger is coming from. My partner and I have been together for 25 years and we have two sons, aged 14 and 16. Both are football crazy and have played since they were very young.
body: However, this side of him rears its ugly head when our kids play matches. He shout s, criticis es and, worst of all, swear s at teenagers. I’m so embarrassed by it and it’s also affecting the boys. Their teammates hear their dad and it’s creating tension. I’ve tried to speak to him about it but he brushes it off. Our boys and the coaches have spoken to him too, but to no avail.

It may sound extreme, but I feel as if I’m falling out of love with him over this. How can I be with someone who shows no respect for his children, their friends and teammates, let alone coaches and referees? I feel he’s being selfish and if he can’t behave decently at matches he simply shouldn’t go.

I don’t think it sounds extreme – it’s a really unattractive side to your partner. This isn’t competitiveness, it’s him being an arsehole and I sincerely hope he doesn’t act like this in other areas of his life.

I went to UKCP-registered psychotherapist Lucy Fuller. We were both interested in the “why now, why here” aspect of this. You say your boys have played since they were young; has he always shouted at them or is this a more recent, or increasing, behaviour?
points: His behaviour is certainly inappropriate, but take a quiet moment to try to find out where the anger is coming from.

articles.title: This is how we do it: ‘At our age we get to wake up and say: What are we doing today? Let’s make love’
articles.summary: A sex podcast opened up a whole new way of communicating for Helen and Ian. • How do you do it? Share the story of your sex life, anonymously. I’ve discovered I like to be spanked – my orgasms have become much stronger.
body: Ian was dating my best friend, Susan, when we met 15 years ago. She invited me around to his house for dinner, and when he opened the door, I thought: oh my god, he’s cute. After they broke up 10 months in and she started seeing someone else, I asked for his contact details and we went on a date. When I called Susan to tell her I was in love, she was totally silent. It was her or Ian. I chose him. It’s one of the best decisions I’ve ever made.

Ian is much more sexual than I am: his love language is physical touch, while mine is quality time. I just don’t think about sex as much as he does. Him wanting to do it more than I do has caused tension, but it wasn’t something we spoke about. Then five years ago, while on a road trip, we put on the podcast Sex With Emily to pass the time. I’d never heard anyone talk about sex like that before. After that, we’d listen to a sex podcast, pause and discuss it, and now we have a dialogue about sex, which has made intimacy so much better. I’ve become more curious and adventurous: I’ve discovered I like to be spanked, and my orgasms have become much stronger because I’m more relaxed.

articles.title: Where to Stay in the Pacific Northwest for a Coastal Fall Getaway
articles.summary: Whether it’s a remote cabin tucked between towering Douglas-firs, or a historic Queen Anne farmhouse in Portland, the Pacific Northwest is the perfect fall getaway—here's where to stay.
body: Chalk it up to my obsession with Twin Peaks, affinity for mossy landscapes, and lifelong fascination with all things misty and mystic; the Pacific Northwest has always felt like a second home. So much so, in fact, that I chose the region for my wedding back in 2024. More recently, I penned a love letter to one of its islands in honor of Practical Magic, and a travel guide to its most famous wine country, the Willamette Valley. The forests are vast, the food is mind-blowing, and the pace is delectably slow—it’s an all-around perfect travel destination, really.

While summers in the Pacific Northwest are characterized by exhilarating mountain summits and paddling along coastal waters, it’s equally appealing in autumn. To state the obvious, the foliage this time of year is downright show-stopping. Plus, you can still hike trails in national parks like the Cascades and Mt. Rainier (and with fewer crowds to boot). Go for a scenic drive, pop into an orchard for a cider tasting, and conclude your day in front of a crackling fireplace. The dream!
points: Whether it’s a remote cabin tucked between towering Douglas-firs, or a historic Queen Anne farmhouse in Portland, the Pacific Northwest is the perfect fall getaway—here's where to stay.

articles.title: Our Legacy CEO Talks Betting on China and Its Biggest Store Yet
articles.summary: Our Legacy CEO Richardos Klarén on expansion in Asia and partnering with China’s luxury concept store Dongliang.
body: “It’s really the next level for us,” Richardos Klarén, Our Legacy’s CEO, says from his office in Stockholm. The stylish Swedish label, which was founded by Jokum Hallin and Cristopher Nying in 2005 (Klarén joined a couple of years later), is embarking on a new phase of expansion. This month, it will open its biggest store yet in Shanghai, China.

But they’re not going in alone. Dongliang, the pioneering multi-brand concept store, will act as Our Legacy’s operational partner in the country. Founded in 2009, the retailer’s business comprises 15 stores across China, as well as lifestyle concepts including a restaurant, a tea house, and a flower shop. Our Legacy already partnered with the retailer as one of its stockists in China, and has a permanent space in its Maison Dongliang location.
points: Our Legacy CEO Richardos Klarén on expansion in Asia and partnering with China’s luxury concept store Dongliang.

articles.title: Your Brussels Sprouts Need a Crispy, Cheesy Skirt
body: It’s That Simple is our series about recipes so easy, you can make them with your eyes closed. Think tiny ingredient lists, laid-back techniques, and results so delicious you’ll text home about them.

Thanksgiving is a marathon, not a sprint. No matter how expertly you time the meal, the sides are rarely eaten straight from the oven. They linger on the table while guests graze, refill their drinks, and share every detail about cousin Charlotte’s dating life. That’s why I gravitate toward easygoing dishes that thrive at room temp.

This year, try my brussels sprouts with a crispy, cheesy skirt. Known as frico in Italian, it’s what happens when you bake grated cheese until it morphs into a golden savory cracker. The texture is lacy and light like a potato chip, shattering at the tap of a spoon or chomp of your teeth. And even with only one ingredient, it’s enough to turn a brussels sprouts skeptic into a full-blown convert.

After removing the brussels from the oven, you might worry you didn’t nail the frico. The cheese will look soft and pliable. Just give it time while you baste the turkey, check those rolls, or take a sip of wine. After a few minutes it’ll harden into a brittle shell.

articles.title: Frico'ed Brussels Sprouts
articles.summary: Brussels sprouts are better with a crunchy Parmesan skirt.
body: A slick of oil and sprinkling of salt are the only adornments brussels sprouts need to shine. But put a crispy Parmesan skirt on them and suddenly the humble veggie becomes the belle of the ball. This recipe does just that. By roasting the brussels sprouts snuggled into a blanket of grated Parmesan cheese, the cheese melts into a crispy, frico-like sheet that clings onto the sprouts, surrounding them in a lace-like halo. It’s a dramatic side dish, but one that makes a serious statement. If roasted correctly, and the stars align in your favor, you can unpeel the entire sheet off in one swift swoop, presenting it as the culinary masterpiece it is. Fans of fun, this is for you.

articles.title: Florence Pugh and Finn Cole Go Red Carpet Official
articles.summary: Supporting Cole at the London premiere of ‘In the Shadows,’ Florence Pugh made a compelling case for a softly, softly approach to complementary couple style.
body: Finally! Florence Pugh and Finn Cole have made it red carpet official. The couple stepped out together at the BFI London Film Festival premiere of Cole’s latest film, In the Shadows, with Pugh taking a break from promoting East of Eden to support her boyfriend. And while they didn’t exactly opt for matchy-matchy dressing, their respective looks spoke to a quietly complementary approach to couple style.

Pugh, who has been delighting in a particularly romantic streak of red-carpet dressing of late, wore a gown from Wiederhoeft’s spring 2027 collection, styled by longtime collaborator Rebecca Corbin-Murray. She accessorized with silver Aquazzura sandals, a Bulgari Wild Pop necklace and high-jewelry earrings, and a constellation of delicate diamond piercings by Maria Tash. Hair by Hyungsun Ju (replete with bow-like half-up half-down style), shimmering makeup by Celia Burton, and nails by nail artist Dawn Sterling (A.K.A. Nailglam ) completed the look sweet and sensual look.
points: Supporting Cole at the London premiere of ‘In the Shadows,’ Florence Pugh made a compelling case for a softly, softly approach to complementary couple style.

articles.title: Forget Ferrari Red: Kim Kardashian Pulls up to the Paddock in Pastel Pink
articles.summary: Supporting Lewis Hamilton at the Singapore Grand Prix, Kim Kardashian opted for a look that brought together body-conscious dressing and a sporty sensibility.
body: Forget Ferrari red. Kim Kardashian is making a case for pastel pink in the paddock. The reality star and Skims founder touched down at the Singapore Grand Prix this weekend to support boyfriend Lewis Hamilton, bringing a little feminine energy to the Formula 1 circuit.

Kardashian opted for a sheer, rose-quartz turtleneck maxi dress from Alaïa’s spring 2024 collection, accessorized with black cat-eye sunglasses and a pink Hermès Mini Kelly replete with silver charms. With its leotard-like underlayer and sheer, sweeping maxi skirt, the look was an interesting amalgamation of Kardashian’s style signatures: body-conscious, sporty, and overtly feminine. A more romantic vibe for the paddock—which tracks, given her more loved-up appearances with Hamilton recently.
points: Supporting Lewis Hamilton at the Singapore Grand Prix, Kim Kardashian opted for a look that brought together body-conscious dressing and a sporty sensibility.
